## 2. Symptom (observable) + reproducibility profile
- **HLK (Windows Hardware Lab Kit \u2014 Microsoft's HW certification suite)** **"Connected Standby IO Stress"** (8 hr, Driver Verifier on) fails with **"Multiple BSOD"** `[confirmed]`.
- Bugchecks observed: **`UNEXPECTED_STORE_EXCEPTION (0x154)`** and **`KERNEL_DATA_INPAGE_ERROR (0x7A)`** `[confirmed, Comment 3]`. **No dumps generated** — storage not responding at failure.
- **Earliest capture was a HANG, not a clean BSOD:** GDHM dump `3235882136` (2025-12-12) is a **forced/debugger-break dump** (`BUGCHECK_CODE 0`) of a hung system — GDHM's “Bsod / `0x0_nt!SwapContext`” label is only the capture mechanism (analyzed via bsod-copilot `BSOD0xE2-guide.md`; see §5f). So the failure presents as **both** timeout/hang dumps **and** the 0x154/0x7A clean bugchecks.
- Failure lands **during S0ix entry or exit**; OS recovery succeeds a few times, then a later recovery fails → **soft hang or bugcheck** `[confirmed, Comment 10]`.
- **Heisenbug:** with **WinDbg attached, passes 3/3**, no dumps collectible; one soft-hang seen after detaching `[confirmed, Comments 3–5]`.
- **Reproducibility gates (all [confirmed], Comment 10):**
  - UFS = **primary** storage (NVMe-primary + UFS-secondary → **no repro**).
  - **Windows 25H2** only (24H2 clean).
  - Clean OS **+ Gfx + Wifi** drivers installed (clean OS alone → no CS asserted → no repro).
  - Failure rate **100%** in the failing HLK config (ticket header).

## 3. Initial triage — first discriminators
- **Rule-in (it IS this):** HLK CS IO-stress on **UFS-primary / Win25H2**; a **SCSI READ(06)** hits a **10 s unit-timeout** (`SRB.TimeOutValue = 0xa`); FTH/VISA show the READ **never reached the UFS IP**; OS runs a **hierarchical reset** (`storufs!UfsResetBus` → `storport!RaidAdapterResetBus`); recovery **fails on the SK hynix** device.
- **Rule-out (it is NOT this) — state the exact condition:**
  - Needs PKGC? **NO** — repros with **PKGC disabled** `[confirmed, Comment 10 #5]`. **← key discriminator vs Pattern P1 (`ufs-fabric-timeout-on-pkgc`, 16027585017), which is PKGC-gated.**
  - Boot-time PMC-stuck / IP_ready? **NO** — not a boot/fuse-pull hang → **not P2** (`ufs-fusepull-cdc-race-on-boot`, 16029205689).
  - UFS PHY **signal marginality**? **NO** — repros at **0 dB, −3.5 dB, −6 dB** CTLE equalization `[confirmed, Comment 9]`. *(This ruled out PHY **signal-integrity** as the trigger — distinct from the M-PHY **link-startup** failure seen during recovery (`DME_LINKSTARTUP` PHY err `0x10`, §5g/§7), which is real; eq-tuning does not fix the ~10 s no-response.)*
  - UFS PGCB sequencing? **NO** — repros with PMC PGCB WA at **20 ms / 30 ms** `[confirmed, Comment 9]`.
  - Link-gear marginality? **NO** — repros at **Gear 3** as well as Gear 4 `[confirmed, Comment 10 #6]`.
  - UFS HW hang? **NO** — UFS resumes normally after the eng-driver breakpoint releases `[confirmed, Comment 11]`.
  - Known **LPSS / bugcheck-`0x9F`** issue? **NO** — removing the **LPSS driver** (to rule out the known `9F` UFS issue) still repros (`0x154`); one setup also **hung at `01CS` post code** `[confirmed, Comment 3]`.
- **Nearest look-alike:** P1 — same platform/UFS-primary/S0ix surface and the same `storufs!UfsResetBus` OS reset path, but **P1 needs PKGC and shows `IS_` SBFES/HBFES OCP-fabric errors**, whereas this repros PKGC-off with the transaction **lost above PSF0 and no fabric error**. **Deciding tell:** PKGC-disabled still fails **and** VISA@PSF4/PSF0 shows **no** UFS-side transaction/error.

## 5. Fault evidence & instrumentation (machine-readable evidence map)

### 5a. WinDbg — OS reset path `[confirmed, Comments 8 & 11]`
| command / namednode | field | value @ fault | inference | rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dt SRB _SCSI_REQUEST_BLOCK` | `+0x014 TimeOutValue` | `0xa` (10 s) | SCSI **READ(06)**, QueueTag `0x03` unit-timeout | decisive |
| `kv` stack | call site | `storufs!UfsIntelLkfResetBus → UfsResetBus → storport!RaCallMiniportResetBus → RaidAdapterResetBus → RaidUnitHierarchicalReset → RaidHierarchicalResetWorkRoutine → nt!IopProcessWorkItem` | OS ran full **multi-tier reset** (LUN → abort → device → **bus reset**) | decisive |
| dump `16029462685_UFS` | type | **breakpoint** (eng driver), not a bugcheck | failure caught **at UFS reset**, not a HW fault | useful |

> **Recovery-sequence note `[confirmed, Comment 11]`:** the **abort uses the same SRB → inherits the same 10 s timeout**, so a failing abort just burns another 10 s before escalating. And the OS cannot simply toggle HCE and ring the doorbell — **every HCE toggle must follow `LSS (Link Startup) → PMC to HS-G4 / PWM-G1 → data transfer`** before any new transaction; the driver waits for that reset+link-startup to complete before restarting IO (link state is outside the OS). This is exactly why a device that leaves the link *up* (SK hynix, §5d) derails the recovery.

### 5f. Hang dump — bsod-copilot / `BSOD0xE2-guide.md` (GDHM 3235882136) `[confirmed, Log.txt + comment.txt]`
Analyzed the earliest capture (2025-12-12, ~35 min uptime, WCL, BIOS `WCLPFWI1.R00.3463.D04...`) with the
**bsod-copilot** `0xE2` forced-hang methodology, by interpreting the existing `!analyze -v` (`Log.txt`,
10k lines) + the analyst's `!pnptriage`/`!irp`/`!devnode` notes (`comment.txt`) — the **dump file is on the
remote GDHM share** (not local), so guide-over-existing-kd-log, not a fresh Analyze-Dump.ps1 run (`kd.exe`
v10.0.26100.4188 IS installed and the bsod-copilot toolkit is wired).
| probe | observed | inference | rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| `!analyze -v` | **`BUGCHECK_CODE: 0`** (`ERROR_CODE 0x80000003` breakpoint), bucket `0x0_nt!SwapContext` | **not a bugcheck** — a **forced dump of a HANG** over a connected debugger (bugcheck = capture mechanism, per 0xE2) | decisive |
| `!pnptriage` thread | System PnP device-action worker blocked **~22.06s** (`Ticks 1412`): `KeWaitForSingleObject → storport!RaidBusEnumeratorIssueSynchronousRequest → GenericInquiry → VisitUnit → RaidAdapterEnumerateBus → RescanBus → QueryDeviceRelationsIrp → PnpDeviceActionWorker` | a bus-rescan **INQUIRY** to the UFS unit never completes → PnP worker wedged | decisive |
| `!irp` (pended) | `IRP_MJ_PNP / IRP_MN_QUERY_DEVICE_RELATIONS` on `\Driver\storufs` | OS is re-enumerating the UFS bus when it wedges | decisive |
| `!devnode` | `PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_4D47` ServiceName `storufs`, State **`DeviceNodeEnumeratePending`**, StateHistory **flapping** `Started(0x30a)↔EnumerateCompletion(0x30f)↔EnumeratePending(0x30e)` | UFS devnode in a **re-enumeration loop** (corroborates repeated D0/D3 recovery) | high |
| victim thread | second System thread blocked `ExpWaitForResource → CmpLockRegistry` (registry lock); many pending **wait-wake S0/S4** power IRPs | the enumeration wedge **cascades** → registry/PnP/power pile up → whole-system hang | high |
> **Interpretation:** the **enumeration-path** face of the same fault — a synchronous request to the UFS
> device (here the PnP **INQUIRY**, not a SCSI READ) hangs because the device/link won't answer, wedging
> PnP and cascading to a system hang. Directly analogous to the 0xE2 guide's **USB4 D-state ping-pong**
> (device D3→D0 flapping) + **PPM gate-stall** (one worker wedged, others pile up). It's the earliest
> evidence face (pre-dates the eng-driver-breakpoint SCSI-READ captures) and explains the generic
> `0x0_nt!SwapContext` “timeout” hang bucket. Provenance: GDHM `3235882136`; not attached to HSD.
>
> **Reproduced (2nd hang dump, 2025-12-22, comment 1667202197):** same wedge (~**29.5s**; devnode
> started→enumerate-pending window ~**7 min**), plus two discriminators: (1) at the hang the UFS devnode is
> **PowerDeviceD0** and `!storadapter`=**Working** → **rules out power-gate/D3** (device is *on*, just won't
> answer the INQUIRY); (2) the stall reaches the **filesystem** — an NTFS USN-journal worker
> (`Ntfs!NtfsCheckUsnTimeOutWorker → ExAcquireResourceExclusiveLite`) is blocked behind it. Two captures 10
> days apart ⇒ **repeatable signature**, not a one-off.

## 6. Debug flow (diagnostic narrowing)
1. **PHY signal marginality?** Swept CTLE eq (0/−3.5/−6 dB) and PGCB WA (20/30 ms) → still repro → **ruled out PHY signal-integrity + PGCB as the *trigger*** (§3). *(Early framing was “SW flow”; the deeper 16029462685 dump analysis (step 7) refined it — the trigger is a **HW-side ~10 s no-response** and recovery fails at **M-PHY link-startup, PHY err `0x10`**.)*
2. **Device hung?** Eng-driver breakpoint at UFS reset; UFS resumes fine after release → **not a HW hang**; the problem is a **lost SCSI READ** (§5a/§5b).
3. **Where is the READ lost?** FTH + VISA@PSF4/PSF0 show **no txn at UFS**, none pending → **lost above PSF0** (D2D/compute) → **Issue #1**, root cause open (§5c).
4. **Why hang, not retry?** On timeout OS runs **hierarchical reset**; for **SK hynix**, Endpoint Reset leaves **link up / `IS_` clean / `DP=1`**, steering OS onto a path that **doesn't HCE-toggle** → link never re-inits → recovery **spins the UTRLDBR/UTRLCLR loop** (§5b) → **soft hang** → **Issue #2**.
5. **Confirm vendor dependency:** Samsung sets **`IS_.DFES` + link-lost (`DP=0`)** → OS HCE-toggles → recovers (§5d). Difference is the device's reaction to Endpoint Reset → **spec-implementation gap**.
6. **Fix probe:** MSFT **private driver** that **resets controller (HCE toggle) after `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` & `DME_RESET`** → **soft hang no longer reproduces** on Samsung **or** SK hynix (§8).
7. **Deeper dump analysis (16029462685):** storport `!storloglist` + UIC log pin the mechanism — trigger = a SCSI cmd with **no HW response ~10 s** → hierarchical reset → bus reset → **`DME_LINKSTARTUP` fails, PHY err `0x10`** (link won't re-init). Analyst: **check HW side**; breakpoint hit **6×**; **silently recovers** in normal operation (§5g). This is what reframes step 1's “SW flow” into **“HW-side trigger + SW/vendor recovery gap.”**

## 7. Root cause (precise mechanism + class)
> **Full picture — one story in two stages (HW trigger → SW/vendor recovery gap):**
> **① Trigger (Issue #1, OPEN, HW-side):** a single SCSI command — a **READ** (data path) *or* an **INQUIRY**
> (enumeration path) — gets **no UFS response for ~10 s** (the READ is lost *above PSF0*, never reaching the
> IP). This is the root fault; the analyst says *“check from HW side why it hung.”* It **silently
> self-recovers in normal operation** (eng-driver breakpoint hit **6×**, same pattern) — the visible HLK hang
> is only its *tail*.
> **② Recovery (Issue #2, ROOT-CAUSED):** the 10 s timeout → OS hierarchical reset → **bus reset**, where the
> M-PHY link **fails to re-initialize** (**`DME_LINKSTARTUP` PHY err `0x10` ×5**, `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` fails) →
> the device never re-enumerates → the enumeration INQUIRY wedges → PnP/NTFS/registry cascade → whole-system
> hang. Whether this failing path is taken is **vendor-gated**: **SK hynix** returns from Endpoint Reset
> **link-up + `IS_`-clean** (storufs skips the clean HCE-toggle/link-startup → hits the PHY-fail path);
> **Samsung** returns **link-lost + `IS_.DFES`** (storufs HCE-toggles, re-inits, recovers). **Fix:** MSFT
> driver forces the full HCE-toggle re-init unconditionally. *Detail below.*

- **Issue #2 [root-caused]:** UFS **device reaction to `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` differs by vendor**. **SK hynix** keeps the **link up** with **`IS_` clean (`DP=1`)** after Endpoint Reset, so the Windows `storufs` recovery path **does not toggle HCE / re-init the link** and recovery **fails → soft hang**. **Samsung** reports **link-lost + `IS_.DFES`**, which drives the **HCE-toggle** recovery path (UniPro §8.2.6/§8.2.2) that **succeeds**. → **spec-implementation gap between vendor devices and the OS recovery flow.** Contributing protocol smell in FTH: the recovery path issues **`DME_ENABLE` (UICCMD `0x39`)**, which the IP databook says is **not permitted** `[fth-snap]`. **Fix** = OS-driver change to always **HCE-toggle after `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` & `DME_RESET`**.
- **Issue #1 [open]:** a **SCSI READ(06) is lost above PSF0** (never reaches UFS IP) causing the 10 s unit-timeout that *initiates* recovery. Root cause **unknown**; separate HSD (ID not stated); path suspected D2D boundary / compute die; CFI trace pending.
- **Recovery fails at the M-PHY layer `[confirmed, 16029462685]`:** once the OS escalates to **Bus reset**, the storufs driver's UIC sequence shows **`DME_LINKSTARTUP` failing repeatedly with a PHY hardware error (`ErrorCode 0x10`)** and **`DME_ENDPOINTRESET` failing** — the **M-PHY/UniPro link will not re-initialize**, which is the concrete mechanism by which enumeration/recovery stalls (§5g). The analyst frames the *trigger* as a **HW-side** problem: a SCSI command (READ or INQUIRY) gets **no response for ~10 s**; in normal operation the platform **silently recovers** (breakpoint hit 6×, same pattern) — so the visible HLK hang is the tail of a pre-existing, usually-invisible fault.
- **root_cause_class:** Issue #2 → **spec-gap** (device-fw vs OS-recovery); the *fix* lands in the OS driver. Issue #1 → **unknown**.
- **Why the naive recovery derails `[confirmed, Comment 11]`:** after `DME_ENDPOINTRESET`/`DME_RESET` the OS must re-init via **HCE toggle → `LSS → PMC to HS-G4 / PWM-G1 → data transfer`** before any new IO. When SK hynix leaves the **link up + `IS_` clean**, storufs skips the HCE-toggle/LSS path and rings the doorbell against a half-reset link → the UTRLDBR/UTRLCLR spin → soft hang. The fix forces the HCE-toggle+LSS sequence unconditionally.

### 7b. Fingerprint registers (high level)
- **`HCS.DP` (bit 0)** — `0` Samsung (link lost) vs `1` SK hynix (link retained): the branch selector for the OS recovery path.
- **`IS_.DFES` (bit 11)** — **set on Samsung, clear on SK hynix** after Endpoint Reset: the presence/absence of the fatal-error status is what routes the OS onto the recovering vs hanging path.
- **`IS_.UDEPRI` (bit 1)** — flags the `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` event.
- **`UTRLDBR` (0x58) / `UTRLCLR` (0x5C)** — the doorbell/clear pair the recovery loop pounds.
- **`UICCMD` (0x90) = 0x39 (DME_ENABLE)** — the databook-prohibited command seen during recovery.
- Full bit-level decode (offsets, access, enable bits, spec text) → add to `reference/ufs-glossary.md` and link here.

## 8. Fix & verification (or workaround + status)
- **Actual PV-unblock disposition (origin bug 14026588381 fields):** a **Manual errata `#288262`, valid till Aug 31 2026**, was provided to **unblock the HLK/WHCK test** — explicitly *“not a fix but an errata to unblock PV; Intel still needs to debug and fix the unit-timeout issue for future platforms.”* `workaround_type=temporary`, `fixed_in_version=Manual errata #288262`, `closed_reason=3rd_party`; **closed by pakumars 2026-02-15 (ww08)**. Note: **`#288262` is a separate manual errata**, *not* the cloned errata-writeup `13014563592` (which never finalized — see §10).
- **Issue #2 (engineering fix):** **MSFT private/eng driver** — controller reset (**HCE toggle**) inserted after `DME_ENDPOINTRESET` & `DME_RESET` in the recovery flow → **original soft hang not reproduced** on **both** Samsung & SK hynix in HLK `[confirmed, Comment 13]`.
  - **Productization:** under MSFT discussion — they may accept only a **smaller interim change**; tied to the current **“2x2”** driver ask. An **ACPI-based variant** was discussed (Klein) but “does not exist today in any of our platforms.”
- **Issue #1:** still **open** — SK hynix vendor engaged to explain device behavior (sync target **WW8.2'2026**); feedback given to MSFT; IOunit-timeout understanding to be **tracked in a separate HSD**. The errata explicitly defers this to a **real fix for future platforms**.
- **Disposition:** sighting `rnavinku` **closed** RC'd as **spec-implementation gap between vendor devices and OS** `[confirmed, Comment 16]`; origin platform bug closed **`complete / workaround`** via the manual errata (`sysdebug_forum`: “WW07 MSFT provided manual errata, closing as known errata”).

## 9. Retrospective (avoidable? prevention? detection gap?)
- **Dead-ends / false leads (do not rechase):** UFS PHY CTLE eq, PMC PGCB WA, link gear (G3), "UFS HW hung", and **PKGC** (repros disabled) — all disproven (§3).
  - **"UFS flash doesn't respond to UFS bus reset"** (early HW hypothesis, Comment 7) — **contradicted** by Comment 11: UFS resumes fine after the breakpoint releases, so the device is not stuck; the lost READ never reached UFS in the first place.
  - **Known LPSS / `0x9F`** issue — ruled out by removing the LPSS driver; still repros (Comment 3).
  - **Clean OS-from-ISO baseline** (Comment 7) — no repro, but only because CS isn't asserted without Gfx/Wifi drivers; not a fix, just confirms the trigger needs the driver stack.
- **Detection gap:** only surfaces on **Win 25H2** + **UFS-primary** + **Gfx/Wifi drivers** + the exact HLK concurrency (RapidFileVerify + CS + SCSICompliance); clean-OS and manual inbox-driver mimics did **not** repro → put this **specific concurrency** in the default validation matrix.
- **Prevention:** validate **vendor-device Endpoint-Reset behavior** (link-lost + `IS_.DFES` vs link-up + clean) against the OS recovery flow **before** qualifying a new UFS device; add a check that the OS recovery HCE-toggles regardless of device error-status reporting.
- **Observability trap:** WinDbg-attached masks it; use the eng-driver breakpoint at UFS reset to force a usable dump.

## 12. Debug story

Picture a laptop (WCL-U) that boots Windows from a UFS flash chip — a SK hynix part. Run Microsoft's HLK "Connected Standby IO Stress" certification test on it and, after a while, it blue-screens. But only in a very specific setup: **Windows 25H2** (24H2 is fine), **UFS as the *primary* drive** (swap in an NVMe as primary and the problem vanishes), and the **graphics + Wi-Fi drivers installed** so the machine actually drops into deep sleep. Frustratingly, the instant you attach a debugger to catch it, it stops failing.

The team burned through a lot of dead ends first — worth knowing so nobody repeats them. They pulled the LPSS driver to rule out a *known* UFS bug: still failed. They suspected the flash chip was simply dead and not answering — but no, once they froze it at the right moment and let it go, the UFS came right back, so the hardware wasn't broken. They tuned the UFS PHY signal, nudged the power-gating timing, slowed the link down a gear, and even **turned deep sleep (PKGC) off entirely** — it *still* failed. That last one mattered: an earlier, similar-looking bug (16027585017) only happens *with* deep sleep on, so this ruled that cousin out.

The breakthrough came from a special engineering driver that deliberately stops the system right at the UFS reset so a memory dump could be captured. It revealed the trigger: a single disk **read** command sat for **10 seconds** and timed out — and the traces proved the read **never even reached the UFS chip**. It got lost somewhere upstream, in the fabric between the compute die and the storage. That “lost read” is still unexplained and is being tracked as its own separate bug (Issue #1) — and the engineers were blunt: this looks like a **hardware-side** problem (why does the drive go silent for ten seconds?), not a Windows bug. Tellingly, the breakpoint driver caught the exact same pattern **six separate times, and every time the system quietly recovered on its own** — meaning in normal daily use the platform rides straight through this and you’d never notice; the HLK stress test just happens to catch the rare time recovery fails.

But the timeout is only the *trigger*. The thing users actually see — the hang — comes from **how Windows tries to recover**. When a command times out, Windows runs an escalating reset sequence, part of which is an "endpoint reset" of the UFS link. Here's the crux: **the two vendors' chips answer that reset differently.** Samsung drops the link and raises an error flag, which steers Windows onto a recovery path that fully re-initializes the link — and it recovers. SK hynix keeps the link *up* and reports *no* error, so Windows takes a different path that never re-initializes the link — and the system wedges into a soft hang. You can literally watch this in the storage logs: during the bus reset the driver fires the link-bring-up command (`DME_LINKSTARTUP`) to revive the M-PHY link, and it **fails five times in a row with a PHY hardware error (code `0x10`)** — the physical link simply won't come back. (The subtlety: a correct recovery can't just poke the controller and resume — it has to walk the full link-startup → power-mode → data-transfer sequence first, and SK hynix's "link still looks up" tricks the driver into skipping it.) Microsoft's fix is a private driver that **always** does the full re-init during recovery no matter what the chip reports; with it, the hang stops on both vendors.

There's a second, earlier snapshot that tells the same story from another angle. Right at the start of the investigation, someone caught the machine mid-hang with a debugger attached and forced a dump. It wasn't a real blue screen at all — just a frozen system. What was it stuck on? Windows was **re-scanning the UFS drive** (a routine "are you still there?" check), which sends a simple INQUIRY command and waits. The chip never answered, so that thread sat for ~22 seconds, other work piled up behind it (including a system-wide lock), and the whole machine froze. The drive was also caught **flapping** — repeatedly detected, re-checked, detected again — the same "keeps dropping and coming back" behavior.

The thread tying it all together: **the failure is always "the UFS chip stops answering something Windows is waiting on."** Sometimes that something is a data read (the timeout path); sometimes it's a device-detection INQUIRY (the enumeration path) — two different doors into the same room. Whether they're literally the same incident or two independent ways the same flaky chip can wedge the system is still open.

So it's really **two bugs in one ticket**: an **open** mystery — the read lost upstream of the storage — and a **root-caused** one — the vendor-vs-Windows disagreement over how to recover from an endpoint reset. To unblock certification, Intel shipped a **temporary errata** that waives the test until Aug 2026; a *real* fix for the lost-read is still owed on a future platform.
